streams.reasoning: From Chemistry Plan stream_logic: Alkene in solvent. Flow rate derived from calculation Q_total = 0.5 mL/min.
From Chemistry Plan stream_logic: Cl2 gas. 1.05 equiv relative to 0.2 M * 0.5 mL/min = 0.1 mmol/min alkene. 0.105 mmol/min Cl2 ~ 10.5 sccm (STP). Actual volume negligible at 1 bar.
From Chemistry Plan stream_logic: Aqueous quench. Flow rate matched to liquid stream A for efficient mixing and phase separation.

mixing_order_reasoning: From Chemistry Plan: Alkene solution mixed with Cl2 gas stream first (Stage 1). Quench stream C added after reaction coil (Stage 2). Incompatible pair Cl2/Thiosulfate kept separate until post-reactor.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas DCM solvent to remove O2 (good practice, though not strictly required by plan).
Pre-cool Stream A and Stream C to 0 C using heat exchanger.
post_reactor_steps: Mix reactor effluent with Stream C (Na2S2O3) in static mixer.
Hold for 1 min to ensure complete quenching of Cl2.
Off-gas scrubbing with NaOH or Na2S2O3 solution to trap any escaped Cl2.
chemistry_notes: Electrophilic addition of Cl2 to alkene. Exothermic reaction requires 0 C control. Cl2 is toxic/corrosive; gas dosing via MFC. Quench with Na2S2O3 mandatory. No light required. Gas-liquid mass transfer is critical; small ID tubing and static mixer used to enhance mixing. BPR not strictly required by calculation but recommended for safety and gas solubility control.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation estimated 3.0 min (range 2.0-4.5 min). Batch was 30 min. Flow advantage ~10x. Using 3.0 min based on calculation Step 2.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Gas-liquid system. Using inlet/STP basis as per universal physics rules for gas-liquid feeds. Q_gas is negligible volume-wise at 1 bar, so inlet and in-channel times are nearly identical.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: From Chemistry Plan: 0 C required for selectivity and safety (exothermic).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation Step 8 says BPR not required. However, setting 1 bar BPR to ensure positive pressure for gas handling and safety with Cl2. Solvent bp (DCM ~40 C) > T (0 C) + 20 C, so boiling not an issue.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA preferred for chemical resistance to Cl2 and low temperature. FEP also acceptable but PFA has better chemical resistance.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: From Batch Input: 0.2 M. Maintained for flow.
